name: Seated hip abduction
cue: Lean forward and drive your knees out with your hips.
research: research.json biomech.hip_abduction: seated, torso hinged 30 deg forward off the back pad (v10, science audit A12: the program cue's 30 deg lean; v9 20) (a hip hinge: pelvis tilted, spine neutral), hips 120 so the thighs are horizontal, knees 90 with vertical shins, feet on foot plates that swing with the pad arms, pads on the outer thighs just above the knees, hip abduction 0 -> 40 (v10: the legs start nearly together, knees ~17 -> 73 cm apart), hands on handles at the sides of the seat. Each pad arm hinges on the vertical axis through its hip-joint centre, which is the abduction axis of a horizontal thigh (tools/design/hip_abduction.mjs). Seat pan short (buttocks and proximal thighs) so the thighs sweep over its front corners without sinking in; low lumbar pad ~5 cm behind the sacrum. Primary: gluteus medius (a fan under the iliac crest) plus the upper fibres of the gluteus maximus (glute_max_up), the research primaries; TFL (secondary) is not drawn because it faces away from the camera. Load: a selectorized weight stack in front of the pad arms on a floor beam from the seat base (it rises 0.1 H as the knees spread). (tools/design/loads.mjs) v10: the hip-joint centres stay on the pad arms' axes, so the seat and its pin follow the sit bones (1.6 cm up, 1.2 cm back) when the pelvis tilts the extra 10 deg, and the seat pan is 2 cm shorter at the front so the abducting thighs clear it; the handles sit at the FK grip of the unchanged arm pose (tools/design/hip_ab_ad_v10.mjs).

targets.note: Shoulder flexion is the one research angle not met: 25 deg with the elbow at 20 puts the hands beside the knees, inside the 40 deg sweep of the thighs and pad arms. The seat handles sit just behind the hips instead (flexion -23, abduction 17, elbow 20), which also keeps the forearms clear of the side glutes and of the knees from the rear camera.

camera.note: Research view is high front (az 0-15, el 30). With this rig the gluteus medius faces laterally and back, and from any front view the flexed thighs and trunk hide it (measured mask at the peak: 12 px at az 0, ~80 at az 40, ~590 from behind, 400x400 stage). The joint action is in the transverse plane, so the camera is mirrored to the high rear and then turned 30 deg toward the lifter's right (az 150) and raised 8 deg (el 38): the near side glute and upper glute face the camera broadside, the low lumbar pad sits to the left of the sacrum instead of over it, and the near knee and pad visibly swing out past the hip. No floor plate: the seat post and the two pad-arm axles stand on a short cross base joined to the stack by a floor beam, so nothing runs below the arc into the title.

skinChecks.note: pad stays on the outer thigh
trunk stays hinged forward off the back pad
